content:
Falls are more likely with arthritis and frailty. Knowing what to do can reduce fear.

This guide covers falls response and follow-up. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

If you fall

  • Stay calm and check for injury.
  • Call for help using an alarm or phone.
  • Only get up if you feel able.
  • Keep warm while waiting.

Personal alarms

Pendant or wrist alarms connect you to a response centre. Ask your council about local services.

Falls response services

Some areas have teams that help people who have fallen but are not seriously hurt. Availability varies.

After paramedics or a falls team help you up

  • Joints you landed on may stiffen; keep gently moving within comfort.
  • Seek urgent help for new pain on weight-bearing, confusion, severe headache, or a head injury while on blood thinners.
  • Tell your GP about the fall; you may benefit from a falls assessment.

When to get help

  • Call 999 if you cannot get up, are badly hurt, hit your head, or are on blood thinners and hit your head.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Should I call 999 if I cannot get up?

Yes, if you cannot get up or are hurt.

Do alarms cost money?

Many have a charge; ask your council.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Falls
  • NICE NG249: Falls — assessment and prevention in older people

Educational information for people in the United Kingdom — not a diagnosis or personal medical advice. Charity no. 1218461. Reviewed by Louis Maxwell (HCPC PH128483). Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
